decisions.quote:
Focal inferential test: A significant triple interaction, F(1, 19) = 16.69, p < .002, partial eta
 squared = .47, such that the compatible mappings (Mapping A for English, Mapping G for
 Hebrew) were the fastest.


Reproduction Criteria
 The reproduction team has been provided access to the original dataset A successful
 reproduction of the Rinaldi et al., (2016) results would be a significant triple interaction of the
 above ANOVA, such that the compatible mappings (Mapping A for English, Mapping G for
 Hebrew) will demonstrate the fastest performance.


Reproduction Result
A significant triple interaction was found, F(1, 19) = 6.76, p = .018, partial eta squared = .262.
However, in contrast to the original findings for English conditions (fastest mapping A), in the
reproduction attempt mappings C and D were fastest than mapping A (although not statistically

                                                   2
 different in the post-hoc Scheffè comparisons). The reproduced pattern of the Hebrew conditions
(fastest mapping G) was similar to the original findings (although not statistically different in the
post-hoc Scheffè comparisons).
 Thus, this reproduction attempt of the claim was failed according to the SCORE criteria.
decisions.location: Claim Summary, Reproduction Criteria, and Reproduction Result, pp. 2-3 (lines 44-65)
decisions.reason: This SCORE report is a computational reproduction re-analyzing the original dataset from Rinaldi, Di Luca, Henik, and Girelli (2016, Experiment 3; Cognition, 152, 40-52). Re-running the focal 2 x 2 x 2 repeated-measures ANOVA on the original dataset produced numerical output, but the statistics differed substantially from the original report (reproduced F(1, 19) = 6.76, p = .018, partial eta squared = .262 vs. original F(1, 19) = 16.69, p < .002, partial eta squared = .47) and the English condition pattern failed to recover Mapping A as fastest (mappings C and D were faster than Mapping A), leading the authors to conclude that the reproduction attempt failed according to the SCORE criteria. Under the codebook rules for Axis 1 (outcome_computation), because the analysis ran and produced comparable numbers that did not recover the reported results, the outcome is 'computational issues'.
